Negative binomial regression by IRLS and Newton-Raphson

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits an NB2 regression model with log link, \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta\), by alternating iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for \(\beta\) (with \(\theta\) fixed) and Newton-Raphson for \(\log\theta\) (with \(\beta\) fixed), until the log-likelihood converges. This is the same model and parameterization as MASS::glm.nb(). No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

nbreg(formula, data, offset, control = nbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A model formula, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. Offsets may be given in the formula with offset().

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional offset vector (e.g. log exposure), added to the linear predictor.

control

A list from nbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "nbreg", a list with components including coefficients, theta, loglik, iter, converged, fitted.values, linear.predictors, weights (final IRLS working weights), y, x, offset, terms, and call.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
y <- rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = data.frame(y = y, x = x))
fit$coefficients
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4508058   0.7668655 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.950002
